newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain floods force thousands to evacuate homes.
newsitem.headline: Spain floods force thousands to evacuate homes.

text.p: Floods caused by a week of heavy rains have forced more than 2,000 people to evacuate homes and cut more than 50 roads in southern Spain, regional officials said on Monday.
A search went on in Cadiz province for a man who disappeared when his car slid into the Guadalete river early on Sunday.
The rains had eased by Monday but floods persisted. Rivers burst their banks and inundated villages, roads and fields.
Around 2,200 people were forced out of their homes in the provinces of Cadiz and Seville, local officials said. More than 50 roads were closed due to flooding in the region of Andalusia.

The rains also damaged crops in the south including olives and strawberries. Agriculture Minister Loyola de Palacio surveyed the area by helicopter on Monday but said it was difficult to put a figure on the damage so far.
However, the Andalusian Farmers' Unions said the rains had caused around 75 billion pesetas ($573 million) of damage.
